strategies.name: Swing momentum
strategies.rationale: Large single-window repricings on thin books tend to continue briefly.
strategies.rule: When the observed price moves >= $0.10 within the lookback window in either direction, buy the side the move points to (YES after an up-move, NO after a down-move).

strategies.name: Overreaction fade
strategies.rationale: Sharp spikes on low-volume demo markets often retrace.
strategies.rule: When the observed price moves >= $0.10 in the window, take the opposite side of the move (buy NO after an up-move, YES after a down-move).

strategies.name: Cheap-tail value
strategies.rationale: Long-shot contracts with real liquidity; the payoff is bounded and known.
strategies.rule: Buy YES only when the best YES ask is <= $0.10 and the market has open interest, so the maximum loss per contract is capped at the price paid.

strategies.name: Rich favourite fade
strategies.rationale: Capped upside on the opposite side; tests whether favourites are overpriced.
strategies.rule: Buy NO when the best YES bid is >= $0.90, i.e. fade a near-certain outcome that is priced at or above $0.90.

strategies.name: Liquid mid-range
strategies.rationale: Tradable two-sided markets; avoids paying wide spreads.
strategies.rule: Buy YES at $0.35-$0.65 only when both sides of the book hold >= 100 contracts and the spread is <= $0.04.
